Mariapocs Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Máriapócs, Hungary

Not demolished. Jews are recorded in Máriapócs from 1770; the community lost independence in 1855, joining Nyírbátor's larger congregation, and later affiliated Orthodox following the 1867 Jewish Congress schism. Population fell from 223 (1840) to 87 by 1941, before deportation to the Nyíregyháza Ghetto and Auschwitz left only about 3 Jews in the village by 1949. This cemetery appears on an 1870 cadastral map, though few tombstones survive; two dated 1940 confirm use into that year. The Heritage Foundation for Preservation of Jewish Cemeteries fenced the site in 2011.
